learning_objective: 🎯 The Grand Finale! Take all your accounting records and summarize them to find out if the business made a profit and what its true financial position is.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: This account shows the result of buying and selling goods. You put 'Direct Expenses' here (wages, carriage inwards, factory power). The result is Gross Profit or Gross Loss.

You transfer the Gross Profit here and deduct all 'Indirect Expenses' (office rent, salaries, advertising, depreciation). The final result is the Net Profit or Net Loss, which goes directly to the owner.
It is a statement (not an account) showing the financial position on a specific date. The left side shows Liabilities + Capital, and the right side shows Assets. Both sides MUST tally!
This means arranging assets and liabilities in a specific order: either in the order of 'Liquidity' (most easily converted to cash first) or 'Permanence' (longest lasting assets first).

fun_activity.title: 📦 Direct vs. Indirect Sorting
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you make and sell t-shirts. Buying cotton, paying the tailor, and factory electricity are DIRECT expenses (Trading A/c). Paying the showroom salesman, printing flyers, and office AC bills are INDIRECT expenses (P&L A/c). Can you sort them?

exam_tips: 📌 Closing Stock appearing INSIDE the Trial Balance goes ONLY to the Balance Sheet (Assets side). (If it is outside, it goes to Trading A/c and Balance Sheet).
📌 'Wages and Salaries' goes to Trading A/c. But 'Salaries and Wages' goes to P&L A/c. Look at the FIRST word!
📌 Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) = Opening Stock + Net Purchases + Direct Expenses - Closing Stock.
quick_recap: ⭐ Financial statements provide a summary of profitability and financial position.
⭐ Trading A/c deals with direct factory/production costs to find Gross Profit.
⭐ P&L A/c deals with indirect office/selling costs to find Net Profit.
⭐ The Balance Sheet tallies based on the Accounting Equation (A = L + C).
